title.narrative: Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project

description.narrative:
The project will improve the performance of provincial water utilitiess and expand access to safe piped water supply and sanitaton for urban residents in small towns in the Lao PDR. The project will contribute to the government's urban sector targets - 90% coverage for piped water supply and 100% coverage for sanitation by 2030 by improving sector coordination and policy implementation in corporatization, improving nonrevenue water management and expanding water supply in povincial towns, developing new water supply systems in small towns, enhancing community action in urban water supply and sanitation and strengthening capacity for project implementation and operation and maintenance.
The project impact will be expanded access to quality and reliable piped water supply and sanitation services for the urban population in the Lao PDR. The outcome will be improved performance of participating water utilities in delivering sustainable water supply and sanitation services.

title.narrative: 11 Oct 2013 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/project-puts-clean-water-tap-towns-across-lao-pdr
Grant 0604: 90% of contracts awarded and 82% disbursed as of 24 Apr 2025
Loan 3041: 95% of contracts awarded and 93% disbursed as of 24 Apr 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: As of 31 March 2025, the overall implementation progress (combined of both WSSP-Loan 3041 and WSSP-AF Grant0604) is 88%, compared to the project elapsed time 89%. The project has major issue lies with the noncompliance of financial covenants of the PNPs due to inadequate tariff revenues to achieve the required financial ratios. It experienced slow implementation of 2 subprojects (Sanamxay and Namthouam). The project is rated For Attention due to pending non-compliance with FM requirements and slow disbursement.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Jul 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45301/45301-002-apfs-en_5.pdf
Some results are in the Initial Environmental Examination | Dec 2020: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45301/45301-002-iee-en_5.pdf
Some results are in the Resettlement Plans | Apr 2021: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45301/45301-002-rp-en_5.pdf
Some results are in the Safeguards Due Diligence Reports | Aug 2022: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45301/45301-002-sddr-en_0.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Dec 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45301/45301-002-smr-en_6.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: The progress of output 1 is 92.3%. The sector coordination meetings were conducted with government stakeholders to discuss preparation of Water Supply and Sanitation Development Strategy (2021-2030), draft standard operating procedure to facilitate water supply system operations, Corporate Plan (CP) and water tariff structure were updated for 8 provincial nampapas. The progress of output 2 is 83%. 7.The project has completed the expansion of the water supply system in New Namtha, Pakxan, Xayabury, and Xamneua. The remaining two towns, Lamam and Samakkhixay, are scheduled to be completed by June 2025. The project has achieved the installation of 248.8 km of water supply distribution pipelines. The progress of output 3 is 97.2%. The project has successfully completed the construction of seven new water supply systems and installed over 112 km of water distribution pipelines in seven towns. The remaining two towns, Sanamxay and Namthouam are scheduled to be completed by June 2025. The progress of output 4 is 90%. 10.The project successfully achieved its target of having 35% female representation, with 404 out of 1,146 members assigned as village development committee members to manage VEI activities. Additionally, the project completed the construction of 193 public toilets and developed sanitation regulations for 15 towns. It also provided 647 sanitation grants to support 249 female-headed households and improved over 13,700 meters of village access roads with drainage. The progress of output 5 is 92%, The project has successfully completed 18 training courses under the capacity development plan, with 336 participants, of which 123 (36.61%) are female and 204 (94%) are female staff from 8 PNPs.
Tenders and Contracts Awarded: https://www.adb.org/projects/45301-002/main#project-tenders
